newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins steady, shrug off Eurobond plans.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins steady, shrug off Eurobond plans.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds were little changed in early trading on Tuesday and dealers said the market had shrugged off Russian plans to issue another Eurobond in the near future, and was focusing more on emerging market and U.S. Treasuries trends.

First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday Russia plans to return to the international capital markets soon with a dollar bond. The bond, running for at least five years, would be issued through SBC Warburg and JP Morgan.
"Such news does not lead to any moves because we are more interested in what is going on in the U.S. economy," a Russian bank dealer said.
MinFins closely track Brady Bonds and other emerging market debt. Speculation over a possible U.S. interest rate hike in May are pressuring emerging market prices.
Dealers said impact was unlikely later today when Western traders step in.
